title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore East (Early and partial Late Show) on 1970-01-03
venue: Fillmore East (Early and partial Late Show)
source: SBD:MR> DAT> Cass.> DAT > CDRPLUS:1. Sound improved on d1t02 (Me & My Uncle)2. SBE's corrected and checked, new md5's generated.

ai_review.summary: Superb Jan 3 1970 Fillmore East soundboard captures a high‑energy set with Pigpen‑driven first half and fireworks on The Other One and Alligator in the second.
ai_review.review: The recording is a classic 1970 SBD that sounds clear for its era, with only occasional mix quirks and minor cuts. Musically the show is a fan favorite – a powerful opening with Morning Dew and Pigpen’s HTH/Alligator, followed by a second‑set surge highlighted by The Other One, Cosmic Charlie and tight jams that keep the band in top form. Reviewers repeatedly note the band’s fluid playing and standout moments throughout.

ai_rating.rationale: Nearly all 18 reviews award five stars, praising both performance and soundboard quality; only minor recording complaints appear, keeping the overall rating very high.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Generally clear and crisp for a 1970 SBD; reviewers call it "very good for the time period" and "Super 70' Soundboard!". A few note occasional cuts (Cryptical Outro) and that Phil's bass sits low in the mix.

show_quality.setlist_flow: First set dominated by Pigpen‑centric numbers (Morning Dew, Here Comes Sunshine, Alligator) with high energy; second set builds from The Other One into extended jams, featuring Cosmic Charlie and tight transitions that keep the momentum soaring.

band_member_comments.Jerry: His vocal on Uncle John is described as "like it's his last time" and his guitar tone noted as perfect by reviewers.
band_member_comments.Phil: A few listeners feel Phil's bass sits a bit low in the mix, though overall playing is praised as fluid.
band_member_comments.Keys: Tom Constanten’s organ flourishes are highlighted as distinct and a key part of the sound, especially on Pigpen‑driven tracks.
